actions.action: Prune mostly brown, yellow, or dead leaves at the petiole base with clean shears
Place the plant in bright, indirect or filtered light and watch for scorched, crispy patches
Check soil moisture with a finger before watering
Water thoroughly when the top 2-5 cm of soil is dry and let excess drain
Feed with balanced liquid fertilizer every 4-6 weeks in spring and summer
Repot every 2-3 years or when roots circle the pot or grow out of drainage holes
Make sure the pot drains well
Wipe dust off the leaves occasionally
If large and healthy but not blooming, give the plant more sun

reason: The answer frames the plant as healthy and mentions old lower-leaf damage and pruning only tentatively. It limits pruning to mostly dead leaves rather than the damaged ground-touching leaves the poster cut, and nothing it suggests is harmful.
